resources.string: AWSOpenVPN — Created by MR.TRYCATCH @ CODEMARVEL INDONESIA

A modified build of OpenVPN for Android for AWS Client VPN profiles with SAML sign-in (auth-federate): the sign-in opens in the browser, and the VPN can be limited to selected apps (Tiny Container, Termux, Tryminal, browsers). Adds an import guide and an Indonesian interface.
Based on OpenVPN for Android by Arne Schwabe, licensed under the GNU GPL v2. The original credits and licences are listed below; the source code of these changes is available from the author.
Why a custom build instead of the stock OpenVPN apps?

The AWSOpenVPN icon (an orange shield with a keyhole and a small cloud) was designed by MR.TRYCATCH @ CODEMARVEL INDONESIA. It exists only to tell this app apart from OpenVPN for Android when both are installed. It is not meant to replace the original OpenVPN for Android logo, designed by Helen Beierling and credited below, and it is not the logo of OpenVPN Inc. or Amazon Web Services.

AWSOpenVPN is a derivative work of OpenVPN for Android (ics-openvpn) by Arne Schwabe and is therefore distributed under the GNU GPL version 2 or later, with the OpenSSL and Apache-2.0 linking exceptions (see the full licences below). Anyone who receives this app may use, study, change and share it; whoever distributes it must also provide the complete source code, including these changes, and keep the licence and copyright notices. OpenVPN is a trademark of OpenVPN Inc.; AWSOpenVPN is an independent project and is not affiliated with OpenVPN Inc., Arne Schwabe or Amazon Web Services.

Choose an OpenVPN configuration file (.ovpn or .conf).

• Standard OpenVPN profiles with certificates, keys or username/password inside the file are supported.
• AWS Client VPN profiles with SAML sign-in (auth-federate) are detected automatically: when you connect, the sign-in page opens in your browser and the VPN starts after you sign in.
• By default an AWS profile only routes the private network for Tiny Container, Termux, Tryminal, Chrome and Edge; change it under Edit → Allowed apps.

In the file picker, use the system Back button or gesture to cancel.
